reason: A: the headline runs right into the stacked decorative circles in the top-right corner. The body copy wraps into a cramped three-line block jammed against the CTA, and the bottle nearly touches the top and bottom edges, so the whole banner feels overstuffed. B: it reads more cleanly left to right with the circles moved to the left edge, but the SOLSTICE logo sits high and doesn't line up with the bottle. The one-line subcopy is small and runs close to the right edge, and the CTA is centred under the text column, leaving a dead gap below the logo.

A is a uniformly shrunk copy of the original. The order and hierarchy survive, but the logo wordmark, eyebrow, body copy, the 'Reserve a Case' label and the legal line are all too small to read at 300x250, and there is dead space under the CTA. B reflows into two columns and keeps the headline legible, but the body copy is now far larger than the CTA. The button and 'Ships late June' are shrunk to a tiny cluster on the right next to an unreadable legal block, so the CTA is buried and the hierarchy is inverted. B also appears to drop the 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow and leaves the divider floating. Both are broken, and A is slightly less bad because the CTA still reads as the focal action.

A reads left to right (logo/ribbon, then product, then headline and CTA) and keeps the can at a fair size, but a decorative dot sits on the logo wordmark ('SOLST CE'), the ribbon is oversized and competes with the headline, and the headline is fairly small. B gives the headline and CTA strong hierarchy, but the can has shrunk to a trivial size and is pushed against the bottom-left edge. The ribbon is tiny and jammed against the headline, and the legal text is crammed beside the CTA with a dot overlapping it, so the left column feels arbitrary and empty.

A keeps the original's centred stack and hierarchy, but it is cramped vertically: the headline sits about 25px from the top, the gap between the subline and the CTA is tight, and the CTA nearly reaches the bottom edge. It reads more like the original squeezed than rearranged. B blows the headline up to almost the full canvas width, so its side margins are only about 30px. It then pushes the subline (now an awkward two-line wrap) and the CTA into a right-aligned bottom row that shares no axis with the centred headline. This leaves a dead bottom-left corner, jams the CTA against the right edge and makes the headline dominate far more than in the original.

A keeps headline, subline and CTA as one group, but the headline runs almost to the side edges and breaks badly ('little' alone on a line). The subline is jammed under 'sunshine.' with no breathing room, and the oversized CTA leaves a dead strip at the bottom. B has the same cramped five-line headline. Its subline floats alone in a large gap, cut off from both the headline and the button, and is set smaller. The CTA sits pressed near the bottom edge, so the stack reads as scattered pieces rather than a deliberate column.

A: the left edges don't line up. The logo and headline start at ~88px, the subcopy at ~70px and the second pill row at ~106px. The CTA floats off to the right, the pills are staggered over two rows with no clear logic, and there is a slightly loose gap above the pills. Still, the vertical spacing uses the canvas reasonably and the hierarchy holds. B has the same ragged subcopy and pill-row edges and adds a third: Blood Orange starts at ~65px, out of line with everything else. The CTA is pushed hard to the right and the pills are jammed right under it, leaving ~80px of dead space at the bottom, so the layout is top-heavy and less intentional than A.

The two candidates are nearly identical shrinks of the leaderboard. In both, the 'New botanical sparkling, out now.' subline and the 'NEW' pill text are tiny (about 6–7 px), and the can icon's label can't be read. A's 'Try It' button is a larger, rounded pill with readable text, close to the original. In B, the CTA has become a smaller, squarer box with cramped, tiny 'Try It' text, which weakens the call to action and loses the pill shape of the brand's button.

A has a real layout, but the can is broken. It is blown up with no fill, so it reads as an empty outline, and its cream circle is cut off alone in the bottom-left corner. The headline is small for this canvas, the copy has big gaps between lines, and NEW floats on its own. B keeps the brand intact, but it is just the original strip placed across the middle. Big empty bands sit above and below it, and the logo circle and CTA press against the side edges, so it does not fit the format at all.

A splits the badge row: FREE ENTRY sits alone under the date while ALL AGES/TASTINGS float above the RSVP. Its flaws are tiny badge text, a smaller headline, an empty bottom-left quadrant and a CTA pushed out to the far right edge.

A has a clean left-to-right banner: the quote, attribution and quote mark share a left edge, and the circle is cropped off the edge as in the original. But the quote text is small for the format, the logo is tiny and indented off the text edge, floating above dead space, and the can sits off-centre toward the top-left of the circle. A keeps the attribution at a readable size and the quote wraps cleanly, but the backdrop circle is pulled fully inside the canvas instead of bleeding off the corner, so it reads as a floating disc that crowds the attribution, and the can is shrunk until its label can't be read.
